There is one shared mechanism behind all of it — one commit scope captured before the operation and resolved against the working tree afterwards — which the round commit also reuses to normalize the line endings of exactly those files, and `commitChanges` now takes one single list of the relevant paths instead of the two overlapping path options it had before. Because the relevant paths are derived from git itself, a file ignored through `.gitignore` (such as the `.env` which `ptbk coder init` writes) can never end up among them, so scoping the commit cannot break on an ignored path.

-   United the DNS configuration manuals of the Agents Server. The DNS records of one server used to be spread over three different manuals with three different visuals: the generated project domains had their own indigo panel on `/superadmin/servers` without any Cloudflare wizard, the server domain got a separate amber panel right below it and only when its DNS was already broken, and the email records lived in a third manual on `/admin/email-server`. An administrator setting up a fresh server therefore had to walk three pages and paste the Cloudflare API token more than once. Now `/superadmin/servers` shows one manual per server which lists **everything the server needs at its DNS provider** — its own domain, the generated project domains, and its email — and configures all of it with one Cloudflare API token in one click. The manual is shown for every server, not only for a broken one, so the setup can also be reviewed and re-applied at any time. There is exactly one DNS component left, `<DnsRecordsInstructions/>`, which renders a list of DNS sections; a subpage passes only the sections which belong to it, so `/admin/email-server` keeps its email records in the same component and the same wizard and points to the Servers page for the complete setup. Each section may offer alternative setups — the generated project domains still offer the wildcard or single-project and the CNAME or A record variants — and the selected variant of every section feeds the one shared Cloudflare wizard. The wizard, its zone-file export and the `/api/admin/dns-records/cloudflare` endpoint now work with record groups instead of one flat record list, so a manual mixing required records (email) with alternatives (server and project domains) still writes exactly the recommended record of each alternative and never both sides of a conflict; duplicate records shared by two sections are written only once. DKIM records intentionally stay on `/admin/email-server`, because their public keys are generated by Stalwart and must not be invented.

-   **Breaking:** Replaced the `--reverse` flag of `ptbk coder verify` with `--order <from-earliest|from-latest|random>`. The old flag only toggled between the two possible directions, which left no room for a third one; the new option names the order explicitly, so `ptbk coder verify --reverse` becomes `ptbk coder verify --order from-latest`. `from-earliest` stays the default and walks the prompt files from the oldest one, `from-latest` walks them from the newest one, and the new `random` shuffles the queue, which is useful when a long verification session keeps stopping on the same prompt files. Because the prompt files are reloaded after every single verification, `random` really reshuffles on each pass instead of picking one order for the whole run. The supported orders, their descriptions and their validation live in one shared definition used by the CLI command, its `--help` output and the standalone verification script, so the CLI refuses an unknown order with the list of the supported ones and the script refuses it with a branded error. The local VS Code coder terminal and the `ptbk coder` landing page were updated to the new option.

-   Added an in-progress signal to `ptbk coder`. A prompt used to jump straight from not started `[ ]` to fully implemented `[x]`, so a queue running for hours never showed which task was being worked on and a coder which was killed or crashed left no trace of the interrupted task at all. Now the prompt file itself carries the intermediate `[^]` status, which is rewritten before every single step of the round, so it always names the harness, the model, the thinking level, the steps which already finished with their price and duration, and the step which is running right now — for example `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress ``, then `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing in progress ``, and finally the unchanged `` [x] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.2036 10 minutes; Testing 35 minutes ``. Only the verified `[x]` state is committed, because the round commit is still created after the prompt has been implemented and verified. The `[^]` status is deliberately never reverted: a killed process, an internal error or any other interruption leaves it in the prompt file as the signal that this task was left in the middle, and such a prompt is not picked up again automatically. The in-progress and the done status lines are built from one shared formatter, so they can never drift apart; the `ptbk coder server` board shows a left-behind `[^]` prompt in its **In progress** column with a `[^]` tag, and `ptbk coder verify` no longer offers a file containing an interrupted prompt for archiving. Because the harness reports its authentication method only when a step finishes, the `(ChatGPT account)` part appears as soon as the first coding step is done. The `ptbk coder` landing page documents the new status.

-   Added a running indicator to the Agents Server **System** menu. While a standalone VPS self-update is in progress, the **Super Admin → Update** entry is now decorated with small spinning arrows, so a super admin sees a running update straight from the menu instead of having to open `/superadmin/update`. The indicator follows the same route-based registry pattern as the existing administrator warning triangles: one shared indicator renderer now draws both the warning and the running state, and the running state is resolved server-side only for the super admin, so nobody else learns about VPS operations. Whether a self-update is really in progress is decided by one shared `isVpsSelfUpdateJobRunning` check, which the update launcher and the installed-version cleanup use as well, so a job whose installer process died without writing its final status is not reported as running.

-   **Breaking:** Removed the `COMPONENT`, `WALLET` / `WALLETS`, `MEMORY` / `MEMORIES`, `USE BROWSER`, `USE DEEPSEARCH`, `USE SEARCH ENGINE`, `USE SPAWN`, `USE TIMEOUT`, `USE TIME`, `USE EMAIL` and generic `META` commitments from the Book language without any backwards compatibility. `COMPONENT` describes the UI that runs the agent, and wallet, memory, browsing, deep search, web search, timeouts, current time, and e-mail are capabilities of the Agent Server which every agent gets anyway, so none of them belongs in the agent source; `USE SPAWN` was unused. The commitment folders, their tool definitions, tool functions, runtime adapters and system-message aggregation were deleted, together with the `USE` system-message aggregation step, the browser / search / e-mail / timeout / memory / wallet **agent capabilities** shown on agent profiles, the matching entries of the New agent wizard (including its e-mail setup step and translations), and the `USE EMAIL` extraction which the Agent Server used to derive per-agent e-mail configuration from the agent source — e-mail sending is now resolved for every agent from the [user wallet](apps/agents-server/src/utils/useEmailSmtpWalletConstants.ts) alone. The generic `META <TYPE> <content>` catch-all is gone as well: only concrete `META` commitments are commitments now, so `META TITLE`, `META AUTHOR` or any other free-form `META` line is no longer parsed. Because of that, `META DESCRIPTION` (whose definition already existed but was never registered), `META FULLNAME` and the low-level `META ID` are now first-class commitments with their own definitions, which keeps agent descriptions, display names, and permanent ids working exactly as before. `fetchUrlContent` moved from the `USE BROWSER` commitment to [`src/scrapers/_common/utils/fetchUrlContent.ts`](src/scrapers/_common/utils/fetchUrlContent.ts) because it is a scraping utility used by the Agent Server `run_browser` tool and the `/api/scrape` route, and the Agent Server keeps all of its own runtime features — the browser tool, `send_email`, `spawn_agent`, user memory, user wallet, and chat timeouts — since they are server functionality rather than agent source syntax. The Book language documentation, the standalone Book language markdown, the commitment dictionary, the specs, the READMEs, the VSCode grammar, and the bundled default agent books were updated accordingly.

-   Added the `N*M` notation to `--count` of `ptbk coder generate-boilerplates`, which now controls not only how many prompt files are generated but also how many prompts are written into each of them. `--count 10*7` creates 10 files with 7 prompts each, while a plain `--count 10` keeps the previous meaning and is treated as `--count 10*1`. The default is `5*1`, so one generated file contains exactly one prompt instead of the four identical copies it used to contain, and the `coder:generate-boilerplates` script which `ptbk coder init` writes into `package.json` uses `--count 5*1` as well. More than one prompt per file is an advanced option: every single generated prompt is one separate coding task, so each of them is separated by a `---` line and reserves **its own fresh emoji tag** instead of sharing one tag with the rest of the file. A `--count` value which is not one or two positive integers is now refused with an actionable error instead of silently falling back to 5 files, the `--count` parsing is shared by the CLI command and the `generate-prompt-boilerplate` repository script, and the `ptbk coder` landing page lists the new notation among the advanced features.

-   Added `ptbk coder ping`, which sends one tiny dummy prompt through a selected harness and model — for example `ptbk coder ping --harness openai-codex --model gpt-5.6-sol --thinking-level xhigh` — and reports the answer of the harness, the measured response time and the usage the harness reported for it. The ping is built on the very same runner the coding queue uses, so it really exercises the configured harness, model, thinking level and authentication (including the rate-limit retry behavior) instead of only checking that the harness command is installed. Besides testing that a connection works and how fast it answers, it is meant to be run **before** you actually need the harness: the tiny prompt starts the hourly/weekly quota window, so the refresh clock is already running by the time the real coding starts. The dummy work needs no tool and explicitly forbids reading, writing or changing anything, and both temporary artifacts the ping creates are removed again, so the project is left exactly as it was — nothing is written, changed or committed. `--no-ui` streams the raw harness output instead of the compact result, and `--allow-credits` behaves as in `ptbk coder run`. The `ptbk coder` landing page documents the new command among the advanced features.

-   Added `--commit`, `--auto-push` and `--auto-pull` to `ptbk coder init`, `ptbk coder add`, `ptbk coder generate-boilerplates` and `ptbk coder verify`. These commands change project files but used to leave the result uncommitted; now `--auto-pull` pulls the latest changes before the command changes anything, `--commit` commits what the command created with the coding-agent git identity, and `--auto-push` pushes that commit to the remote repository. `ptbk coder verify` applies the synchronization around each single verification, so archiving a finished prompt file and appending a repair prompt are committed and pushed one by one instead of at the end of the whole session. All four commands share one implementation of the pulling, committing and pushing, a repository without any change is never committed as an empty commit, and `--auto-push` without `--commit` is refused with an actionable error. `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server`, which already commit every successful round by default, are unchanged. As part of this, the temporary commit message file which `ptbk coder` writes inside the project is now always kept out of the created commit, so a project which does not keep the Promptbook temporary directory out of version control is no longer left with a dirty working tree after committing.

-   Optimized the startup time of the `ptbk` CLI utility. Simply running `ptbk about` used to take several seconds because the published bundle eagerly loaded the heavy third-party dependencies of the whole engine — `jsdom`, `@mozilla/readability`, `@openai/agents`, `openai`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `@azure/openai`, `jszip`, `socket.io-client` and `prompts` — even for commands that never touch them. These packages are now imported on first use through one shared `createLazyModuleLoader` utility, so a command pays for a dependency only when it really uses it; the repository scripts load `typescript` and `pg` the same way. Every command, option and output stays exactly the same; the website scraper, the OpenAI AgentKit tools, the LLM providers, the `.bookc` archive reader/writer, the remote client and the interactive prompts just load their SDK at the moment they need it. Measured on the generated `@promptbook/cli` bundle, `ptbk about` dropped from about 4.6 s to about 1.8 s, which is roughly 2.8 s saved on every single `ptbk` invocation.

-   Optimized standalone Agents Server self-updates. The request-aware root layout now declares its dynamic boundary before static prerendering can start database-backed work, CLI-owned release builds no longer write unusable multi-gigabyte webpack filesystem caches, retained release caches are reclaimed before deployment, and each update phase records its elapsed time in the installer log.

-   Fixed Agents Server ElevenLabs text-to-speech configuration to use only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`; support for the legacy `ELEVEN_LABS_API_KEY` environment variable was removed.

-   Added `--test-before <no|yes-and-fail|yes-and-fix>` to `ptbk coder run`. Pre-coding verification is disabled by default, can stop the run with the complete test output when existing tests fail, or can create and run one shared-format repair prompt before the normal coding queue; an explicit `--test` command is used when provided and `npm test` is the default for the enabled modes. The Coder landing page and local VS Code coder terminals now document and use the repair mode.

-   Fixed preventive generated-project DNS guidance in Agents Server **Super Admin → Servers**. Every registered server now shows the preferred wildcard CNAME record for all current and future project hostnames before its first project is assigned, while assigned project domains remain listed with the shared setup guidance.
-   Fixed the self-contained Agents Server Stalwart mail service health check so it verifies the public `mail.<domain>` hostname resolves to the VPS, rather than reporting only local API, bridge, and inbound-hook configuration as operational. `/admin/email-server` now flags stale/misconfigured inbound-mail DNS with the detected addresses and fills its copyable A records from the installer’s known VPS public address. The installer now asks for the canonical `mail.<domain>` A record and domain MX record together with the web A record, preventing a fresh VPS from being installed with an unreachable inbound mail target.

-   Added a configurable secure-password generator to the Agents Server `/admin/users` create-user flow. The generator now opens in its own dialog, starts with a secure 16-character configuration (uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters), lets administrators adjust the length and included character categories, and returns the selected generated password to the create-user form. It reuses browser Web Crypto with unbiased sampling, guarantees every selected category is represented, and never permits an empty character set.

-   Fixed Agents Server live chat progress for the default OpenAI Codex local runner. The runner now opts into Codex JSONL events only for Agents Server chats, so the existing progress-card sync can replace the rotating `THINKING_MESSAGES` placeholder as soon as Codex starts a real action. The shared runtime-log resolver turns those events into brief, safe lines such as **"Inspecting relevant files."**, **"Running tests."**, and **"Updated relevant files."**; it deliberately never exposes command text, tool payloads, or private reasoning. Other `ptbk agent-folder` and Codex runs keep their existing human-readable output.

-   Added an Agents Server internal S3 file browser to `/admin/internal-s3`, with folder-style listings under the configured prefix, breadcrumbs, parent navigation, object metadata, and direct file links. Superadmins can switch between the VPS-wide Internal S3 view and the current server's `/admin/files` gallery through shared Storage tabs, while normal admins retain access only to their server's files. The files gallery now uses SQLite-compatible file and agent queries, preventing blank cells, missing dates, and `NaN KB` file sizes.

-   Added `--isolate` to `ptbk coder run`, which keeps the working tree you started the coder from untouched while a task is being implemented. Every prompt gets its own temporary git worktree in `.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/<task-name>` on branch `ptbk-coder-isolation/<task-name>`, with its own copy of the project `.env`, and the coding agent, the `--test` verification command and the round commit all happen inside it. As soon as the task is implemented and verified, it is merged back into the branch the coder runs on as one commit — exactly like a non-isolated round — and the worktree together with its branch is deleted. When the merge fails, the task is marked as `[!]` instead of `[x]`, a commit describing the failed merge and the manual recovery steps is written into the original worktree, the temporary worktree is kept so the changes can be merged by hand, and the coder simply continues with the next task instead of stopping.

    -   `--isolate` now works on Windows. An isolated worktree nests the whole repository below `.promptbook/coder-isolation-worktrees/<task-name>`, so repository paths which still fit into the Windows `MAX_PATH` limit inside the project no longer fit inside the worktree. Git long path support is therefore enabled for every process an isolated run starts, which fixes `error: unable to create file …: Filename too long` followed by `fatal: Could not reset index file to revision 'HEAD'` while creating the worktree. It also fixes the far quieter consequence of the same limit: without it, git reported every too-long path inside the worktree as deleted, so the round commit would have merged mass file deletions back into your branch.
    -   A worktree which still cannot be checked out is now removed again instead of being left half-written, and the failure is reported as one branded error which names the git lines that explain it, instead of thousands of `Updating files: <percentage>` progress lines.

-   Improved the Agents Server **Book language manual**. A manual exported in Czech is now really written in Czech: all manual prose, chapter titles, catalog labels, examples and pitfalls come from language packs resolved by the requested export language (commitment reference bodies stay in their canonical English, because they are the specification of the keywords). The **Execution and compilation model** chapter was removed, deprecated commitments (such as `TEMPLATE`) are no longer documented at all, and low-level commitments (such as `MODEL`) moved into a closing **Low level commitments** chapter that is opt-in through a new, by default unchecked, download option. The PDF export is now branded with the Promptbook logo, claim, accent color and export metadata, renders every `book` code block with the same syntax colors as `<BookEditor/>`, and wraps pages far better: commitment documentation headings are nested under their catalog entry instead of jumping back to chapter level, headings stay with their content, and long code blocks may split instead of pushing a third of a page of whitespace.

-   Upgraded the **Cloudflare setup wizard** in every Agents Server DNS record manual from step-by-step retyping to two batch imports, so an administrator no longer configures the records of `/superadmin/servers` and `/admin/email-server` one at a time. **Import with API token** writes every shown record into the matching Cloudflare zone with one click using a pasted `Zone.DNS` token (or the `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` already configured on the VPS) and reports per record whether it was created, updated, already configured, skipped, or rejected. **Import zone file** generates a downloadable BIND zone file for Cloudflare's **Import and Export** screen without any credentials. Both ways share one batch plan, so placeholder values such as `<VPS_PUBLIC_IP>` and record alternatives are never written automatically and are listed with the reason instead; existing conflicting Cloudflare records are never deleted, and only records which can hold a single value per hostname (`A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, and matching policy `TXT` records) are overwritten. The manual steps and the propagation check remain available as a fallback. The Cloudflare API client is now shared between the Agents Server and the `sync-vercel-domains` script instead of existing twice, and it translates `MX` priorities and `CAA` values into the structured fields the Cloudflare API expects.

-   Fixed the self-contained **Stalwart Mail Server**, which never received a single management call. The VPS installer bootstrap, the administrator provisioning, the domain/alias/MTA-hook synchronization, and the `/admin/email-server` health snapshot all addressed `http://127.0.0.1:8080/api`, a path Stalwart does not serve, so every call answered HTTP `404`; Stalwart therefore stayed in bootstrap mode without any SMTP listener and no agent could send or receive mail. All management calls now use the JMAP management endpoint that Stalwart publishes as `apiUrl` in `/jmap/session` (`http://127.0.0.1:8080/jmap/`). The installer defines that endpoint once and reuses it for the bootstrap request, the administrator provisioning, and the `PTBK_STALWART_API_URL` value, while Agents Server upgrades an already-persisted legacy `/api` path (or a bare Stalwart base URL) so existing installations recover without a manual `.env` edit. The inbound MTA hook is now also registered with the millisecond response timeout Stalwart expects instead of a `30s` string. **Synchronize Stalwart** on `/admin/email-server` and **Synchronize all domains** on `/superadmin/email-server` now share one button component that reports an unreachable or still-bootstrapping mail service next to the button instead of replacing the page with a Server Components error.

-   Added automatic harness installation checks to `ptbk coder`. Before `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server` start, and at the end of `ptbk coder init`, Promptbook now detects whether the used harness command is installed globally and compares its version with the newest one published to npm; when a harness is missing or outdated it offers to run `npm install -g <package>@latest`. One shared harness registry describes the command and npm package of all supported harnesses (OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cline, Claude Code, Opencode, Gemini CLI), `ptbk coder init` checks OpenAI Codex and Claude Code, and non-interactive terminals only print the manual installation command.

-   Added standardized expandable project chips to Agents Server chat. Agent `[[project]]` references now show their running state and open a compact menu with **Open the project in a new tab** and **Open the project page in a new tab** actions; profile-preview, private-mode, and durable chats reuse one runtime-enriched project reference model and shared markdown-chip renderer. **Every** way an agent mentions its project renders as that same chip now, not only the `[[project]]` token: a link into the project page or into an internal project file such as `/agents/yznzwhgnqpinl1/projects/prague-murders-map/files/index.html`, and the public project URL such as `https://prague-murders-map.live.ptbk.io/` written as a link or as a bare URL, are all replaced by the chip, so the chat shows the **project name** (`Prague Murders Map`) together with its running state instead of a raw URL, and the internal file path is never linked — opening the project from the chip always uses its public URL. A project name without a README heading is humanized for the chip label, so `prague-murders-map` reads as `Prague Murders Map`. One reference model carries the URL prefixes which identify a project, and the shared markdown renderer matches them case-insensitively against link targets and bare URLs, ignoring encoding and trailing slashes, while images, code and links to other projects stay untouched. Because the public project URL is now resolved from the persisted project-domain assignment instead of only from a live runtime, a stopped project is recognized and named as well — its **Open the project in a new tab** action stays disabled until the project runs.

-   Improved Agents Server Book language manuals: downloads now create a standalone PDF or Markdown manual from the selected server agents, use those agents' real Book sources as examples, and put their actually used commitments first. The Documentation toolbar now has one **Download manual** action with format, language, and included-agent options; clearing every agent produces the portable generic manual.

-   Unified Agents Server administrator warning indicators in the **System** menu. A single route-based warning registry now drives the top-level **System** triangle, affected category labels, and individual menu entries, keeping them in sync. In addition to existing resource-monitor, core-agent, Shibboleth, and Agent Projects DNS states, the menu now flags registered-server DNS problems, VPS and per-server email health, and active self-contained S3 failures. Warning details remain gated to the matching administrator or super-admin capability, so regular and anonymous users receive none of these operational states.

-   Fixed Super Admin server renames so saving a name on `/superadmin/servers` also updates that server's `SERVER_NAME` metadata. The metadata write now runs in the explicitly selected server context rather than the administrator's current-server context, preserving isolation across a multi-server VPS; it updates existing SQLite metadata rows reliably and clears stale metadata caches.

-   Added a guided **Cloudflare setup wizard** to every Agents Server DNS record manual. The shared panel now walks administrators through opening the correct Cloudflare zone, adding the existing record-table values with the provider’s field names, using **DNS only** for directly verified A/AAAA/CNAME records, and checking propagation; the record table remains the single source of truth for both server and email DNS instructions.

-   Added the selected `--thinking-level` to successful `ptbk coder` prompt status lines, alongside the harness and model (for example, `by Claude Code \`claude-opus-4-8\` thinking \`xhigh\``). The Coder landing page now documents this completion metadata.

-   Fixed standalone VPS project DNS visibility: `/superadmin/servers` now verifies generated project hostnames, defaults its setup guidance to the preferred wildcard CNAME record, and labels each owner with a linked agent chip. DNS problems now also appear on affected project pages and the **Agent Projects** menu item.

-   Simplified Agents Server project runtimes to one automatic Run action: projects with a non-empty `package.json` `dev` script now run `npm run dev`, while all other projects use the static server. Admins can now run and stop projects directly from `/admin/projects`.

-   Enhanced the Agents Server `/superadmin/environment` editor so super admins can add arbitrary valid `.env` variables directly from the UI. Every variable already persisted in the VPS `.env` file is now listed automatically — including integrations such as `ELEVEN_LABS_API_KEY` — while sensitive values remain masked and the server-side super-admin-only write policy remains enforced.

-   Fixed the Agents Server home page so the temporary federated-agents loading section is not shown before federation data is available. When no federated servers or agents are returned, the homepage now remains free of that section instead of briefly showing it.
-   Fixed cross-platform unit-test portability: macOS canonical temporary paths no longer conflict with test assertions or Git exclusions, shell-script links normalize Windows-style separators on every host, document-scraper unit tests no longer require locally installed Pandoc or LibreOffice, import repair handles Windows paths when run on another platform, and Agents Server builds clear stale Next route types left by another build output directory.

-   Fixed the Agents Server home page so the temporary federated-agents loading section is not shown before federation data is available. When no federated servers or agents are returned, the homepage now remains free of that section instead of briefly showing it.

-   Unified Agents Server DNS setup guidance. `/superadmin/servers` and `/admin/email-server` now reuse one record-instruction panel with consistent record columns, setup steps, conflict guidance, and DNS-provider documentation links; server-domain diagnostics still offer one compatible A/AAAA/CNAME alternative, while email setup correctly requires every MX/SPF/DMARC/TLS record shown.

-   Improved Agents Server `/admin/users` with a practical admin table that puts named users first and clearly groups anonymous visitor accounts below them. User creation now opens a create-server-style dialog with a browser Web Crypto secure password generator, and every user links to a detail page with recent chat activity plus direct links to filtered Chat history and Task manager views. Chat history now supports preserving a user filter through table, thread, and CSV views, and task/chat tables link back to the relevant user.

-   Fixed the Agents Server initial chat greeting so a partially loaded agent never shows its opaque permanent id. The canonical chat now reuses the already resolved human-readable agent title until the remote agent profile is available.

-   Fixed the default Coder project npm scripts to use the locally installed `ptbk` command expected by the Coder boilerplate verification.

-   Enhanced Agents Server admin page tabs with one shared underline-style navigation component. Configuration, storage, and task-manager scope tabs now use consistent spacing, active-state styling, hover states, and accessible current-page semantics.

-   Unified the Agents Server per-server and VPS-wide task managers. The VPS-wide `/superadmin/task-manager` now shows the same task details, target links, log controls, task detail links, cancellation/retry actions, terminal button, and bulk cancellation action as `/admin/task-manager`, with only the owning **Server** column added; cross-server actions preserve each server's isolated context, and the former `/admin/task-manager-vps` URL redirects to the new super-admin route.

-   Scoped agent project reporting correctly across standalone VPS servers. The per-server `/admin/projects` dashboard remains limited to agents owned by the current server, while the super-admin `/superadmin/resource-monitor` project storage panel now aggregates every registered server and labels each project with its owning server. Project and agent links stay local for the current server and use the owning server's absolute URL for foreign projects, so a VPS-wide report cannot open another server's project under the wrong database namespace.

-   Simplified the Agents Server homepage to keep only the **List** agents view. Removed the Graph, Office, Maze, and Pixel view switcher/renderers, their unused layout/state/test/CSS code, the Pixel Agents asset route, and the now-unused `reactflow` and `pixel-agents` dependencies; the existing list and federated-agent cards remain available.

-   Added **VPS server setup** tasks to the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager`. Creating a new server and the automatic Let's Encrypt certificate obtain/renew maintenance now persist their full task lifecycle, including start, finish, duration, worker, queue, attempt, error, and searchable target details, and the task's **Open** link leads to the super admin `/superadmin/servers` page.

-   Added project DNS setup instructions to the Agents Server `/admin/servers` project-domain panel. Administrators can now choose between configuring one project-specific hostname or a wildcard for all generated project domains, and between an A record pointing to the VPS or a CNAME pointing to the server domain.

-   Fixed the standalone VPS self-update **Total** time in the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` so it reports the real update duration instead of `0s`. A successful self-update restarts the server, which usually terminates the detached installer before it can record its own `FINISHED_AT`; the persisted job snapshot now falls back to the status file's last-write time for such stale runs, and the task-manager row no longer collapses an unknown finish time to the start time (showing `-` instead of a fabricated zero-second total).

-   Linked every Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` task to the page it operates on, and back, as one universal pattern. Each background task now shows an **Open** button that jumps to what it is doing: a **chat completion** or **chat timeout** task opens its chat thread (`/agents/<agent>/chat?chat=<chatId>`), a **VPS self-update** task opens the `/superadmin/update` panel, and a **browser preview** task opens the previewed page in a new tab. The forward link is resolved through a single shared `resolveAdminChatTaskTargetLink` helper reused by both the task-manager table row and the per-task detail page (`/admin/task-manager/<taskId>`), which already shows only that one task. The reverse direction is now complete too: the self-update panel links to its own task in the task manager, and the existing per-message **Task** link on `/admin/chat-history` (chat → task) now reuses the same shared `buildAdminChatTaskDetailHref` builder, so both link directions stay consistent (DRY).

-   Fixed the Agents Server so administrator and super-admin **System warnings** are never shown to — nor delivered to — regular or anonymous visitors. These warnings (server **resource pressure**, a **misconfigured Shibboleth login method**, and **missing core agents**) describe problems only the responsible administrator should act on, but the misconfigured-Shibboleth warning previously decorated the top-level **System** menu with a warning triangle even for signed-out visitors, and the raw Shibboleth activation/configuration status was serialized into every page. Each System warning is now gated behind the matching admin capability through a single shared `resolveHeaderSystemWarnings` policy reused by both the top-level System label indicator and the individual System submenu entries, so the three indicators can no longer disagree or leak. The Shibboleth menu status is now resolved server-side only for administrators (non-admin viewers receive an inert `SHIBBOLETH_AUTHENTICATION_MENU_STATUS_HIDDEN` status), matching how the resource-monitor and core-agents warnings were already withheld from the client, so the warning information is no longer available client-side for viewers who may not see it. Finally, the whole **System** menu — like the **Documentation** menu — is now hidden entirely from visitors who are not signed in, so anonymous visitors no longer see a System entry at all. The separate `/api/auth/shibboleth/status` login endpoint that the login dialog uses to offer the Shibboleth sign-in button is intentionally left unchanged.

-   Added a self-contained **Stalwart Mail Server** to standalone VPS Agents Server installations. Stalwart is installed, bootstrapped with local storage and automatic DKIM keys, started as a system service, and connected to each server through an authenticated DATA-stage MTA hook and local SMTP submission account. Every active agent now receives normalized dotted, compact, permanent-id, and plus-tagged addresses on the server domain; incoming mail creates a dedicated durable chat with an `EMAIL` source flag and a normalized passwordless ad-hoc sender, while the completed agent answer is sent with the agent’s display name, from the exact alias originally addressed, and to all original To/Cc/From participants. Unknown local recipients receive the required apology plus the server’s public-agent directory. Per-server `/admin/email-server` and VPS-wide `/superadmin/email-server` pages expose health, synchronization, aliases, and complete MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC/TLS-RPT/MTA-STS/CAA/PTR guidance, and agent profile/context-menu/QR surfaces now use the same shared address formatter. A backwards-compatible migration extends durable and audit chat-history sources with `EMAIL`, and the VPS installer provisions a normal Stalwart application administrator, removes the temporary recovery credential, provisions transport secrets, and opens only public inbound SMTP port 25 while keeping submission and management local.

-   Added ex-post reinstatement of the bundled Agents Server agents so an admin can restore the default and core agents without recreating the server. There are two kinds of bundled agents: the **normal default agents** (in `agents/default/`) that showcase what Promptbook agents can do, and the **core agents** (in `agents/default/.core/`, such as Adam, Expert, Creator, and Teacher) that are used as the shared base every other agent inherits from. When any of these are missing, admins now see an admin-only notice on the home page — a **warning** for missing core agents and an **information** banner for missing normal default agents — each with a single button that recreates only the missing agents while leaving every existing (possibly edited) agent untouched. The reinstatement reuses the exact same creation logic that runs when a server is first created (a shared "create only the missing agents" helper is now used by both the core-agent seeder and the new default-agent reinstatement). A new admin **Core Agents** page (`/admin/core-agents`, in System → Administration) tracks whether every core agent is present, explains why each core agent exists, links to each present agent's editable book, and shows — for reference only, never as a warning — whether a present core agent differs from the bundled repository version. Missing core agents also raise a warning indicator on the System menu's Administration category. The whole flow is available only to per-server admins (not regular users) and is backed by a new admin-gated `/api/admin/default-agents/reinstate` endpoint.

-   Moved every Agents Server **Super Admin** page from `/admin/*` to a dedicated `/superadmin/*` route root, so the VPS-wide superadmin area is separated from the per-server `/admin/*` administration pages. The nine relocated pages are **Servers** (`/superadmin/servers`), **Environment variables** (`/superadmin/environment`), **Resource monitor** (`/superadmin/resource-monitor`), **Update** (`/superadmin/update`), **Database** (`/superadmin/database`), **Internal S3** (`/superadmin/internal-s3`), **Logs** (`/superadmin/logs`), **Harness auth** (`/superadmin/harness-auth`), and **CLI access** (`/superadmin/cli-access`); each page directory keeps its own components, server actions, and helpers and moves wholesale. The System menu links, the raw-IP first-run `?setup=1` redirect, the post-delete server redirect, the file-upload-unavailable notice link, the shared **Server configuration** and **Storage** tab shells (whose remaining Metadata/Limits/Files tabs stay under `/admin/*`), and every affected `revalidatePath` call now point at the new `/superadmin/*` routes, and `superadmin` is registered as a reserved top-level path so it is never mistaken for an agent name. The backing HTTP APIs are intentionally left at `/api/admin/*` — only the browser-facing page routes changed — and the per-server administration pages (models, metadata, limits, users, files, projects, task manager, chat history, and the rest) stay under `/admin/*`.

-   Fixed the standalone VPS Agents Server so chat completion tasks now run for **every** server on the VPS, not only the first one. On a VPS hosting several servers (for example `lts.example.com`, `lts1.example.com`, and `lts2.example.com`), messages sent to agents on any server other than the first previously stayed pending forever because the background durable-chat worker only ever advanced jobs for the default server: its loopback self-call has no server `host` header, so server routing resolved to the single default table prefix and every other server's queued and running jobs were never claimed or synchronized. The worker's coordinator poll now fans out across **all** registered servers each tick — running expired-job recovery and the local runner inside each server's own routing context via a shared server-context override (an immediate per-message trigger still stays scoped to its own server) — so answers are produced and completed for every server, and one failing server never blocks the others. Added a companion **VPS-wide task manager** (superadmin only, `/admin/task-manager-vps`, linked from the System menu) that aggregates the durable background tasks of every server on the VPS into one read-only table with a **Server** column, reusing the existing per-server task-manager UI and the shared injected-task pipeline; the two task managers are interlinked with **This server** / **All servers (VPS)** tabs shown to superadmins.

-   Fixed the OpenAI Codex sign-in on the Agents Server `/admin/harness-auth` page so admins can actually authenticate the ChatGPT subscription instead of paying per token. The interactive authentication terminal previously launched the bare `codex` CLI, which starts the Codex chat TUI (not a login) and immediately dies in the non-interactive browser terminal with `Session terminated, killing shell...`; the installer now runs `codex login --device-auth`, whose device-code flow needs no local browser callback and works from the embedded terminal. The Harness Auth page now shows a guided OpenAI Codex wizard that explains the difference between the **ChatGPT subscription** (uses the signed-in ChatGPT account quota, no per-token OpenAI API charges) and the **OpenAI API key** (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, billed per token), walks a first-time admin through the device sign-in step by step, and shows which method is currently in use — resolved server-side by reusing the same `Logged in using ChatGPT` detection (now a shared `CODEX_CHATGPT_LOGIN_STATUS_NEEDLE` constant reused by the Codex runner script) that the runtime uses to pick between the ChatGPT account and `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

-   Made Agents Server agent IDs case-insensitive so the same permanent agent id resolves to the same agent regardless of the letter casing used in the URL. For example `/agents/doQMRg82izNfJa/chat`, `/agents/doqmrg82iznfja/chat`, and `/agents/DOQMRG82IZNFJA/chat` now all open the same agent and redirect to its canonical id. Human-readable agent-name lookups stay exact, while permanent-id lookups now match case-insensitively through a single shared `buildAgentNameOrPermanentIdFilter` helper (Supabase/PostgREST `ilike` with `LIKE` wildcards escaped) that the core `AgentCollectionInSupabase` and every Agents Server agent lookup reuse, plus a shared `isSameAgentPermanentId` comparison used by the in-memory route, ownership, and custom-domain resolvers. For example `/agents/doQMRg82izNfJa/chat`, `/agents/doqmrg82iznfja/chat`, and `/agents/DOQMRG82IZNFJA/chat` now all open the same agent and redirect to its canonical id. Human-readable agent-name lookups stay exact, while permanent-id lookups now match case-insensitively through a single shared `buildAgentNameOrPermanentIdFilter` helper (Supabase/PostgREST `ilike` with `LIKE` wildcards escaped) that the core `AgentCollectionInSupabase` and every Agents Server agent lookup reuse, plus a shared `isSameAgentPermanentId` comparison used by the in-memory route, ownership, and custom-domain resolvers.

-   Made the standalone VPS Agents Server manage its Let's Encrypt certificates automatically for every assigned domain, whether the domain belongs to the server or to a project. A new process-wide certificate scheduler periodically runs a lightweight `install.sh apply-certificates` maintenance pass that reuses the existing idempotent per-domain certificate configuration: it obtains a certificate for any domain that still lacks one and renews any certificate close to expiry, then re-renders nginx so freshly issued certificates start serving HTTPS. This means a server created **before** its DNS is configured now gets its certificate on its own once the DNS starts resolving — no manual `apply-domains` rerun needed — and expiring certificates are renewed without intervention. The maintenance pass never restarts the Agents Server, never touches the firewall, and keeps every domain isolated in its own certificate lineage, so a single domain failing to validate (or a project failing to run) can never take the main server domain offline; the raw-IP default server and plain-HTTP fallback keep the server reachable from the web throughout. The failed-issuance warning now points operators at the automatic retry (and the immediate `install.sh apply-certificates` command).

-   Fixed the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` **All** history view so tasks are ordered by finished time, with the newest finished task on top. The `All` view previously ordered rows by last-update time, which let a self-update that finished long ago sit above chat completions that finished more recently. The default `All` ordering now reuses the shared task timeline timestamp (which resolves to `finishedAt` for terminal tasks) in both the SQLite comparator and the PostgreSQL `ORDER BY`, while still-active tasks keep their start/queue placement instead of dropping to the bottom.

-   Moved the standalone VPS Agents Server installer from `other/vps/install.sh` to `install.sh` in the repository root so the entry-point script is easy to find, while its dependency scripts (for example `other/vps/test-nginx-config-generation.sh`) stay under `other/vps/` and are called relative to the root installer. The self-update flow, the installer self-references it persists into `PTBK_VPS_INSTALL_SCRIPT`, the Agents Server installer-path resolver, and the documented `curl … | bash` deploy instructions now point at the root `install.sh`; the resolver still falls back across candidate paths, so servers self-updating from an older release keep working across the move.

-   Fixed Agents Server chat feedback stars so unpicked stars no longer stay yellow. The shared chat feedback controls now render CSS-colored star icons with their resolved color, fill, and stroke state applied through shared CSS variables and inline SVG icon styles instead of the native colored emoji glyph, inactive stars are hollow even when generic SVG styles are present, and the compact response control plus rating modal share the same rating-message key resolution so both reflect the picked rating consistently.

-   Added `--env` to the standalone VPS Agents Server installer. Fresh installs now default to the `preview` environment, while `--env live`, `--env production`, and `--env lts` select the corresponding Promptbook branch and persist it as `PROMPTBOOK_REPOSITORY_REF`.

-   Fixed the standalone VPS Agents Server installer so `curl ... | bash -s -- ...` works under `set -u`. Bash leaves `BASH_SOURCE` empty when executing a script from stdin, so the installer entrypoint now uses a dedicated sourced-script detector and the self-update script-copy step skips the stable-copy rerun when the running installer has no readable file path. The root verification setup now also resolves the same local Agents Server aliases, keeps the CLI build-command unit test mocked at the direct helper import paths, and raises the shared Agents Server production build heap limit after verification exposed a 4 GiB Next build OOM.

-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server multi-server isolation so servers hosted on one VPS can no longer leak agents, projects, metadata, users, chats, or any other server-scoped data into each other. Each registered server now has **its own SQLite database file** (`servers/<server-namespace>.sqlite` next to the existing database), and one **VPS-wide SQLite registry database** (the existing `agents-server.sqlite`) owned by the super-admin holds only the `_Server` list of servers. The SQLite Supabase-shaped adapter routes every table access through a single choke point — VPS-level `_`-prefixed tables go to the registry database while server-prefixed tables go to the owning server's database under clean unprefixed names — so all existing data access code works unchanged. `/admin/servers` create/rename/delete now manages persistent registry rows with stable ids (renaming a domain keeps the server's data; deleting a registration keeps its database file on disk), the `SERVERS` environment variable remains only a projection for nginx/certbot provisioning and Edge middleware host matching, and creating a server no longer overwrites the shared `SUPABASE_TABLE_PREFIX` (the root cause of servers flipping into one another's tables). Domains listed in `SERVERS` are auto-registered into the registry on first boot, so a freshly installed VPS bootstraps itself, and the embedded database admin now targets the current server's isolated database only.

-   Added a **Cancel all active tasks** action to the Agents Server `/admin/task-manager`. A guarded button in the background-tasks header requests cancellation of every active (queued + running) durable chat task across all users in one confirmed, reason-required step via a new `/api/admin/chat-tasks/cancel-all` endpoint, reusing the existing single-task cancellation flow for each task and reporting how many tasks were matched and cancelled.

-   Separated the Agents Server `/admin/chat-history` by chat thread instead of one mixed pile. A new **Chat thread** filter (grouped from `chatId` by a new `/api/chat-history/threads` endpoint) narrows the table view to a single conversation once an agent is picked, and the CSV export honors it. The chat transcript view now lists recorded threads and opens one conversation at a time (never mixing threads) and always renders in bubble mode regardless of the article-mode control-panel preference. The table message column now renders Markdown, and links into chat history (super-admin external-chat banner and admin conversation search results) now deep-link to the most detailed view — the recorded conversation in chat view — when the agent and thread are known.

-   Added sortable column headers to Agents Server administration tables, with shared sorting controls and helpers reused across task manager, chat history, chat feedback, messages, files, images, API tokens, metadata, servers, environment variables, usage detail, Shibboleth, and resource monitor tables. Paginated admin lists now send whitelisted sort fields to their loaders so the full result set is ordered before pagination.

-   Fixed the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard desktop rail so the left panel scrolls independently on short viewports, keeping the stepper and progress controls reachable while preserving the existing fullscreen layout.

-   Fixed the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard so the right content panel scrolls independently inside the fullscreen layout, keeping long Book, knowledge, and test steps reachable without moving the desktop rail.

-   Added a classic Book editor exit from the Agents Server manGo new-agent wizard. A small Book button in the manGo rail now opens the existing classic editor with the current partially created draft, including the generated book text and ready knowledge sources, so users can finish creation outside the manGo flow.

-   Added **Download .book** to the Agents Server agent context menu. The action downloads the stored source book for the selected authenticated local agent using the same safe filename sanitization as book ZIP exports, while the existing inherited-source `/api/book` route remains unchanged.

-   Improved Agents Server chat source chips so JSON-like and binary image citations no longer show raw payload text. Source labels now fall back to compact URL snippets when a source URL is known, or type labels such as `JSON file` and `JPEG image` when it is not; source chips now use semantic SVG icons for websites, JSON, documents, media, archives, and related file types, with URL-backed image citations rendered as thumbnails.

-   Extended runnable Agents Server agent projects with durable public runtime exposure. Project pages and the internal agent-project runtime API can now start dev or static project runtimes, the server persists assigned ports and project subdomains, production Linux runtimes are started as dedicated pm2 processes, and the standalone VPS installer reads the managed project-domain list to configure nginx reverse proxying and SSL certificates. `/admin/servers` now shows project subdomains assigned below each server domain.

-   Fixed standalone VPS Agents Server self-updates so newly required host software is installed through the same shared dependency path as fresh installs. The code-server installer now uses the standalone release installer instead of global npm installation, avoiding the `Please pass --unsafe-perm to npm to install code-server` failure during `/admin/update`.

-   Added super-admin browser VS Code access for Agents Server agent projects. Project pages now show an **Open VS Code** action and support the GitHub-style `.` shortcut for super admins, launching a per-project `code-server` session rooted at the project directory with matching light/dark theme settings, editable files, git tooling, and terminal CWD on the project root. Standalone VPS installs now install `code-server`, proxy VS Code sessions through an authenticated nginx subpath, route `install.sh` on already installed servers into self-update, and share dependency installation between fresh installs and self-updates so new server-side software dependencies are applied during updates.

-   Added runnable local agent projects to the Agents Server. Local agents can now ask the server for a tracked free port, start a server-owned project dev command, or start a static file server for plain project folders; the prompt instructions expose the internal runtime API through environment variables instead of embedding secrets. Project runtime ports now appear in `/admin/resource-monitor` with links to the live port and owning project plus terminate/release controls, and each project page shows whether its project is running or has an assigned port with the same terminate/release action.

-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar preview so the sample now renders the existing shared `AsciiOctopus` canvas avatar directly, matching the web avatar visual instead of the blocky terminal rasterization.

-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar alignment so the web sample now centers the shared animated `AsciiOctopus` lines to the same dashboard width as the surrounding live-terminal boxes.

-   Added persistent per-agent browser profiles to the Agents Server. Every agent now browses in its own isolated Playwright profile (persistent Chromium user-data directory), so cookies, session tokens, logged-in sessions, and other browser data survive across chats and server restarts — for example an agent signed into a social network stays signed in without the user logging in again. The `run_browser` tool resolves the acting agent from the hidden tool runtime context, and the live browser preview (opened from knowledge/citation chips in chat) now runs on the same agent profile via a new `agent` query parameter of `/api/page-preview/stream` threaded through a new optional `agentIdentifier` prop of `<Chat/>`, so when the user logs in somewhere inside the live session the login is saved into the agent's profile for future agent browsing. The profile is managed through the wallet: a new agent-scoped `BROWSER_PROFILE` wallet record type (added by a backwards-compatible migration) stores only the link to the profile directory on the filesystem (default under `.promptbook/agents-server/browser/profiles`, overridable via `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE_STORAGE_DIRECTORY`), it is registered automatically on first agent browsing and editable at `/system/user-wallet`. `BrowserConnectionProvider` now caches one browser context per profile directory and closes contexts with no open pages after an idle timeout (`RUN_BROWSER_CONTEXT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 10 minutes) — the browser is not kept alive while unused, only the profile data stays permanent. The wallet UI and menu are now labeled **Agent Wallet** (records belong to agents, each agent has its own wallet; the `/system/user-wallet` route is kept for backwards compatibility).

-   Enhanced the Agents Server live browser preview (shown when a cited page cannot be embedded as an iframe) into a remote-desktop-like session inspired by Chrome Remote Desktop and AnyDesk. The preview now forwards natural browser interactions to the server-side headless browser — hovering, clicking, double-clicking (click counts are tracked client-side like in remote desktop viewers), dragging and text selection via raw pointer presses and releases, mouse-wheel scrolling, and full keyboard typing including shortcuts (keys outside the US layout fall back to text insertion). A browser-like toolbar adds back/forward/reload, an editable address bar (submitted URLs are SSRF-checked server-side), local zoom (Ctrl+wheel, pinch, or toolbar buttons, 50–300 %), an "Open in new tab" link, and a full screen mode. The remote viewport is sized dynamically: it follows the measured preview area and full screen changes instead of the previous fixed 1280x800. Stream frames are now sourced from a CDP `Page.startScreencast` — pushed on every repaint for smooth video playback and scrolling, idle-cheap, capped at ~15 fps, with a heartbeat that re-sends the last frame so proxies do not drop quiet streams — while the previous screenshot-polling loop remains as a fallback. The input protocol (`src/book-components/Chat/Chat/pagePreview/`) is shared between the new `<LiveBrowserPreview/>` component and the `/api/page-preview/input` route, events are delivered strictly in order with move/wheel coalescing, a new `/api/page-preview/state` route keeps the toolbar in sync with navigations happening inside the page, and a reconnect overlay appears when the stream drops.

-   Fixed `ptbk coder` artificial waits so they are tied to wall-clock deadlines instead of decrementing only while the Node process is actively awake. `--wait-between-prompts`, `--wait-after-prompt`, `--wait-after-error`, OpenAI Codex rate-limit backoff, and Claude Code session-limit resurrection waits now elapse during `p`/web-UI pauses and while the computer sleeps.

-   Fixed Agents Server `/admin/harness-auth` so the page no longer shows multiple xterm panels. Harness status and apply output now render as plain text, and the **Live authentication terminal** is the only interactive terminal, mounted only while an authentication session is running.

-   Renamed Agents Server standalone VPS harness authentication to `/admin/harness-auth`, with Harness Auth menu/page/API copy and installer guidance aligned around `PTBK_HARNESS` subscription-backed CLI sign-in.

-   Fixed the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal avatar so the sample now uses the shared terminal avatar renderer and the same `AsciiOctopus` fallback as the real Promptbook Developer coder agent. The terminal avatar dimensions and refresh cadence are centralized in `src/utils/agents/terminalAgentAvatarVisual`, with both the real rich CLI UI and the landing page using that shared preset.

-   Fixed `scripts/repair-imports/repair-imports.ts` so it preserves imports from modules mocked in the same test file. The repair pass now detects static `jest.mock(...)` and `vi.mock(...)` module specifiers and leaves matching imports on their mocked facade module instead of redirecting them to deeper implementation files, preventing repaired imports from bypassing test mocks.

-   Fixed Agents Server `/admin/task-manager` self-update rows so a successful standalone VPS self-update is no longer shown as failed when the old server process is stopped before the installer writes its final `STATUS=succeeded`. Task-manager self-update snapshots now reuse the same restart-aware target-commit reconciliation as `/admin/update`, and the archived self-update task history stores that resolved success state before a later update overwrites the singleton status file.

-   Updated the `ptbk coder` landing page live terminal so it now plays a one-shot `ptbk coder run` sample that mirrors the real rich CLI dashboard: typed command, shared animated agent visual rendered as colored terminal text, `Session` / `Current task` / `Live output` / `Controls` boxes, and final output without blinking, clearing, or looping. The terminal avatar now uses the shared avatar-to-ASCII rendering pipeline instead of a landing-only drawing.

-   Added the `ptbk coder` landing page app at `apps/coder-landing` (http://localhost:4025/). The dark-mode, mobile-friendly Next.js page introduces `ptbk coder` to developers who know Claude Code or OpenAI Codex: copyable syntax-highlighted terminal samples walk from `npm install ptbk` through `ptbk coder init` to the kanban `ptbk coder server`, an animated fake terminal replays a scripted coding session, the `--agent agents/developer.book` option is demonstrated with the default developer agent in a readonly `<BookEditor/>`, and all six harnesses (`claude-code`, `openai-codex`, `github-copilot`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cline`) are presented as cards with logos, model examples, and shell samples. The footer mirrors https://www.ptbk.io/en and states that `ptbk coder` is a Promptbook subproduct by AI Web s.r.o. The app follows the official Promptbook branding and ships with an `apps/coder-landing/specs/` folder of interlinked markdown specs which serve as the single source of truth for 1:1 replication of the page.

-   Fixed the Agents Server chat source chip for attached images so it shows the original filename (for example `DSC_0139 (2).JPG`) instead of unreadable binary content. Attached files are cited by their content-addressed CDN URL, whose filename is normalized, so the shared citation-label resolver used to download the image and print its first decoded line. Both the durable and private-mode chat surfaces now wrap the resolver with `createAttachmentAwareCitationLabelResolver`, which maps a citation whose URL points to one of the chat attachments back to that attachment's original `name` and only otherwise delegates to the server metadata resolver — which also avoids the needless image download.

-   Fixed `scripts/repair-imports/repair-imports.ts` so cross-boundary imports from `src` to `apps/agents-server/src` can be repaired. The shared project entity scanner can now include app source exports when requested, which lets the repair script resolve Agents Server constants such as `DEFAULT_LOCAL_AGENT_RUNNER_MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS` without broadening the files it rewrites.

-   Added automatic standalone VPS self-updates for the Agents Server. `/admin/update` now exposes `.env`-backed automatic update settings for `PTBK_AUTO_SELF_UPDATE_ENABLED`, `PROMPTBOOK_REPOSITORY_REF`, and `PTBK_AUTO_SELF_UPDATE_CRON` (default `0 0 * * *`) while reusing the shared VPS environment writer used by `/admin/environment`. A Node-runtime scheduler checks the configured branch on the cron cadence and starts the existing zero-downtime self-update flow only when the remote branch is ahead. Persisted self-update jobs now record whether they were started manually or automatically, and both `/admin/update` and `/admin/task-manager` show that trigger.

-   Refactored `ptbk agent-folder run-multiple` so `runMultipleAgentMessages` is now a small watch-loop orchestrator. Active queued-message scheduling, local project summary loading, GitHub repository synchronization, idle auto-pull state, shared dashboard presentation, and path/wait helpers now live in focused private modules under `runMultipleAgentMessages/`, while the exported API, queue selection behavior, retry handling, auto-clone/auto-pull timing, console output, and rich UI state remain unchanged.

-   Refactored the Agents Server standalone VPS self-update utility so `vpsSelfUpdate` is now a small facade. Environment resolution, `.env`/origin configuration, status/log-file persistence, background process launch, overview assembly, git repository reads, candidate commit listing, and stale-job reconciliation now live in focused private modules under `vpsSelfUpdate/`. The exported API, installer invocation, persisted status/log format, update overview payload, and custom commit picker behavior remain unchanged.

-   Fixed Agents Server chat image attachments so clicking an attached image opens an in-chat popup preview instead of navigating to a new browser tab. Non-image attachments still keep the existing new-tab file link behavior.

-   Added `?messageDraft=` quick buttons to Agents Server chat messages alongside the existing `?message=` buttons. A `[Label](?message=...)` button still sends its text immediately, while a new `[Label](?messageDraft=...)` button prefills the composer with an editable draft — focusing the input and moving the caret to the end — so the text can be reviewed and changed before sending. The markdown button parser now recognizes the `messageDraft` link, `<Chat/>` owns the composer prefill through a new internal draft channel (overridable via the new `onQuickMessageDraftButton` prop), and draft buttons are only shown when there is a composer (or handler) to receive the draft.

-   Fixed the `ptbk coder run` rich terminal UI so sessions started with `--limit <run-count>` now show that configured run limit in the Session scope summary.

-   Refactored the Agents Server Shibboleth authentication utility so `shibbolethAuthentication` is now a small facade. The SAML protocol/user constants, shared type contracts, RelayState sanitization and request-detail extraction, configuration resolution (Service Provider URL derivation and Identity Provider metadata fetching and XML parsing), Node-SAML client and Service Provider metadata generation, SAML profile-attribute extraction, prefixed table-name resolvers, authentication-attempt audit logging, and user/identity linking now live in focused sibling modules under `shibbolethAuthentication/`. The re-exported functions and types, the SAML request/response handling, the emitted Service Provider metadata, and the observable authentication and audit behavior remain unchanged.

-   Refactored the Agents Server admin task-manager loader so `getAdminChatTasks` is now a small facade. The SQLite-mode fallback path (raw job/timeout row and user/agent lookup loading, record mapping, in-memory view/search filtering, dashboard sorting, and summary counters) and the PostgreSQL raw-SQL path (the shared union query, the list and counters query builders, and SQL row/counter mapping), together with the shared ISO-timestamp helpers and SQL value coercion, now live in focused sibling modules under `getAdminChatTasks/`. The exported `getAdminChatTasks` signature and `GetAdminChatTasksData` type, the SQLite/PostgreSQL dispatch, the emitted SQL, and the observable task items, counters, and pagination remain unchanged.

-   Refactored the Agents Server server backup ZIP builder so `createServerBackupZipStream` is now a small facade. The shared lazy-loading Supabase context and table loaders, the section dispatcher and per-section exporters (metadata, agents, conversations, users, files, and messages), the manifest builder, the user/agent preview maps, attachment reference indexing, feedback-thread parsing, wallet redaction, binary download, filename generation, and the generic row/value utilities now live in focused sibling modules under `serverBackup/`. The exported `createServerBackupZipStream` signature, the archive layout, the `promptbook-server-backup/v2` manifest, and the observable ZIP contents remain unchanged.

-   Added `--limit <candidate-count>` to `ptbk coder find-refactor-candidates`, so a single run creates at most that many refactor prompts and, when more candidates are found, keeps only the most important ones. Importance is a combined severity score — the sum of `actual / threshold` ratios across every exceeded line-count, entity-count, function-count, and complexity threshold — computed while scanning, so files that overshoot more thresholds (or overshoot them further) are preferred. The limit is applied after skipping candidates that already have prompts and can be combined with `--level`. The positive-integer option parser previously private to `ptbk coder run` was extracted into a shared `createPositiveIntegerOptionParser` reused by both commands, and the VS Code "Find refactor candidates for Coding Agent" terminal now passes `--limit 10`.

-   Refactored the Agents Server local SQLite Supabase adapter so `$provideLocalSqliteSupabase` is now a small facade. The table-schema metadata and resolvers, value serialization/deserialization, mutation payload defaults, PostgREST filter translation, table/index DDL, row-level DML, SQLite error normalization, low-level SQL helpers, and the Supabase-shaped client/table/query-builder classes now live in focused sibling modules under `localSqliteSupabase/`. The public `$provideLocalSqliteSupabase`, `$resetLocalSqliteSupabaseForTests`, and `ensureLocalSqliteTableReadIndexes` exports, the generated SQL, and the observable query behavior remain unchanged.

-   Refactored the Agents Server mocked-chats editor state so `useMockedChatsEditorState` is now a lean state orchestrator. Preset cloning, saved-list lookup/upsert/dirty comparison, list persistence and error resolution, delete confirmation, draft save-flow factories, and the participant/message/settings draft reducers now live in focused sibling modules. The API calls, request payloads, feedback messages, draft mutation behavior, and the `UseMockedChatsEditorState` contract remain unchanged.

-   Refactored the Agents Server export-as-transpiled-code page client so `AgentCodePageClient` is now a small page orchestrator. Transpiler listing, code generation, ZIP download, and agent-profile loading moved behind a focused `useAgentCodeExportState` hook, while the header, source-book viewer, transpiler picker/harness section, export warnings, error banners, and generated-code preview are now separate presentational components. The API calls, request payloads, abort/cleanup behavior, error/loading states, and visible UI remain unchanged.

-   Refactored the Agents Server standalone VPS update client so `/admin/update` now separates overview polling, target environment controls, current deployment metrics, pending commits, and update-job log/status rendering into focused private helpers. The update POST payloads, polling behavior, success/error messages, and visible UI behavior remain unchanged while the top-level `<UpdateClient/>` is now a small page orchestrator.

-   Enhanced Agents Server chat dictation with a failover-backed speech-to-text flow and Wispr Flow-inspired correction loop. The chat input now keeps microphone states clear through start, stop, processing, permission, and error transitions; preserves the original selection for replace-selection dictation; keeps interim transcript text outside the textarea so the caret stays stable; lets corrections update the local custom-word dictionary including capitalization-only fixes; and backtracks only the tracked dictated chunk instead of restoring the whole previous composer value. The provider layer now reports terminal stall failures when no fallback remains, while the existing OpenAI transcription provider and Browser Web Speech fallback stay behind the shared speech-to-text provider abstraction.

-   Enhanced the Agents Server homepage graph layout so server, folder, and agent subsets are placed by a deterministic free layout instead of nested grids. The current server is now centered in the graph, folders and agents keep their React Flow parent boundaries, and inheritance/import/team links are used as layout hints at the server, folder, and agent levels so relationship arrows can pass cleanly through the subset boundaries without flattening the hierarchy.

-   Fixed Agents Server local and external chat-runner queueing so attached files are visible to the answering agent. Runner `.book` files now include the existing chat attachment context for user messages, preserving image/file URLs and best-effort inline text previews for readable attachments before the local or git-backed runner writes the final answer.

-   Fixed Agents Server agent inheritance so local parent agents are loaded directly from the server collection instead of re-entering the authenticated `/api/book` HTTP route. `FROM @Basic` / `FROM {Basic}` now materializes the referenced local parent, agents without `FROM` inherit from the local Adam agent, and `FROM @Void` / `FROM {Void}` still explicitly disables inheritance.

-   Added security PRDs for current Agents Server risks that still need implementation: unauthenticated browser-test automation APIs, missing owner-scoped private agent/folder authorization, and unauthenticated CDN uploads.

-   Leveraged the `spaceTrim` utility for authored multiline strings that were still assembled via array `.join('\n')` or `+ '\n\n' +` concatenation. The `TEAM` commitment's shared teammate-usage guidance, the built-in `ptbk coder` boilerplate template contents, and the `<LlmChatPreview/>` fallback scenario greeting now use `spaceTrim` template literals — producing byte-identical output while improving readability. The now-unused `buildCoderPromptTemplateContent` helper was removed.

-   Fixed `ptbk -v` so it prints the Promptbook version just like `ptbk --version`, while keeping `-v` / `--verbose` available for subcommands that use verbose logging. Added VS Code terminal shortcuts for both version checks.

-   Replaced frozen citation page-preview screenshots in Agents Server chat with live browser previews for sources that cannot be embedded in an iframe. The shared `<CitationIframePreview/>` now opens a Playwright-backed MJPEG stream through `/api/page-preview/stream`, forwards click and wheel input through `/api/page-preview/input`, and keeps the existing iframe path for embeddable URLs. Active live preview sessions are tracked in process memory, closed when the modal stream is aborted, and surfaced as `Browser preview` rows in `/admin/task-manager` without a database migration.

-   Surfaced the standalone VPS self-update session triggered from `/admin/update` as a task row inside the Agents Server admin `/admin/task-manager` dashboard. The task-manager API now reads the persisted self-update job snapshot via a new lightweight `readVpsSelfUpdateJobSnapshot` helper (no git access, safe for admin polling), maps it into an `AdminChatTaskRecord` of the new `VPS_SELF_UPDATE` kind through the shared `mapVpsSelfUpdateJobToAdminChatTask` utility, and prepends the synthetic row to page 1 whenever it matches the requested view/search. The row is labelled "Self-update", counts toward the running / failed-24h summary metrics, and hides the row-level Cancel/Retry buttons because the self-update lifecycle is driven from `/admin/update` rather than the durable chat-task admin API.

-   Changed the Agents Server footer's "Made with ❤️ in Europe" line to show a deterministic positive/neutral emoji derived from the deployment commit hash. The footer now passes the commit-specific emoji through the existing translation placeholder, with a shared `getCommitFooterEmoji` helper and unit coverage for missing SHA fallback, deterministic mapping, and variation across commit hashes.
-   Changed the Agents Server footer version line to show the latest server release tag, the deployed commit short hash when the server is newer than that tag, and the release age linked to the Git repository. The footer now receives cached server-side Git metadata reused from the self-update helpers, keeping the client footer render lightweight.

-   Fixed Agents Server local and external chat-runner queueing so the runner-visible message book for the first durable user turn is assembled through one shared lifecycle helper that prepends the configured `INITIAL MESSAGE` agent greeting and then includes the current `MESSAGE @User` turn. This keeps the synthetic greeting shown in empty chats available to out-of-process runners even though it is not persisted in `UserChat.messages`, while avoiding duplicate local/external thread-building logic.

-   Fixed Agents Server initial book seeding so bundled default and `.core` books honor their own `META VISIBILITY` commitment. The standalone seeder and managed-server bootstrap transaction now omit the explicit default visibility override and let the shared persistence normalization resolve the visibility from the book source first, falling back to `UNLISTED` only when the book does not declare it.

-   Hid Agents Server folders whose name starts with `.` (for example `.core`) from the homepage agents list by default, and added a toolbar **Show hidden** / **Hide hidden** toggle so administrators can opt back into seeing them. The new `filterHiddenFolderTree` utility removes hidden folders together with their descendants and the agents inside them in one pass, so the LIST, GRAPH, OFFICE, MAZE, and PIXEL_OFFICE views stay consistent. The toggle state is persisted in the URL as `hidden=show` (mirroring the existing `view=` query pattern) and the toggle button only appears when the unfiltered organization snapshot actually contains a hidden folder, so workspaces without any `.`-prefixed folder are unaffected.

-   Bumped the default coding model used by the `coder:run` npm script created by `ptbk coder init` from `gpt-5.4` to `gpt-5.5`. The bundled `agents/developer.book` (copied into the consumer project from `agents/default/developer.book` via the existing CLI runtime-asset path resolution in `ensureCoderDeveloperAgentFile`) and the automatic post-init boilerplate generation are unchanged; only the `--model` flag baked into the generated script is updated, so `npm run coder:run` now drives OpenAI Codex with `gpt-5.5` by default.

-   Removed the placeholder **"Working on your request"** title and the **"What I'm Doing Now:"** wrapper from Agents Server durable chat progress cards so the response no longer shows generic headings between the `THINKING_MESSAGES` rotation and the final answer.
